Guileless

GYL-lis · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Guileless describes someone so open and free of cunning that deceiving others -- or suspecting deceit in them -- never crosses their mind.

The guileless intern believed every excuse her coworkers gave her, never suspecting they were taking advantage of her.

Worked Example

The guileless child handed his lunch money to the older boy without a second thought, never imagining anyone would trick him.

Guileless describes someone so honest and trusting that deceit simply doesn't occur to them -- they take people at their word, sometimes to their own disadvantage.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

unsuspecting: Unsuspecting describes a moment: someone simply unaware, right then, that a trick is coming. Guileless is a lasting nature -- a guileless person is open and without cunning always, so the very idea of deceit never occurs to them.

innocent: Innocent mostly means free of guilt or blame -- innocent of a crime, or innocent in the sense of unspoiled. Guileless is narrower: it names a complete absence of cunning, someone too open to deceive anyone and too open to expect deceit.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

cunning: cleverly deceptive

deceitful: intentionally misleading

Where it sits · how easily others could fool them — trusting → guileless → unguarded

trusting vs. guileless: Being trusting just means you give people the benefit of the doubt; guileless goes further -- deceit never even occurs to a guileless person, whether from others or in themselves.

unguarded vs. guileless: Unguarded goes even further than guileless: a guileless person never suspects a trick, while someone completely unguarded has no defenses left at all -- an easy target for any scheme.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — guile

root — guile: cunning, deceit (Old French (guile))

suffix — -less

suffix — -less: without (Old English)

Put it together

Put it together: guile ("cunning, deceit") + -less ("without") = without deceit -- innocent and trusting. (You already met guile itself as a headword earlier in this course.)

Use the root in a new word: beguile

Use the root in a new word: beguile: The same root gives us "beguile," meaning to charm or deceive someone -- guile can be a tool for tricking people, which is exactly what a guileless person can't imagine.

Root Check

Word Choice

Guileless is a warm, slightly literary word -- it works well when describing someone's innocent trust in a way that feels sympathetic rather than critical.
